markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Causal SASRec already represents ordered behavior. Preserve it to isolate whether the objective improves discrimination. (2) A bounded residual can expose recent interests without overwhelming sequence states. Recurrence weighting could instead revive stale demand, so compare it directly with recency pooling. (3) Uniform multi-negative cross-entropy introduces competition among candidates. Its benefit remains an empirical question under the pinned evaluation.

**Related-work insights.** (1) gSASRec identifies problems with negative-sampled BCE; Scalable Cross-Entropy motivates informative candidate competition. Together they support testing the objective first [1–2]. (2) VISTA supports candidate-specific history extraction. A small residual attention branch offers a feasible adaptation, although Amazon gains and compatibility understanding remain unproven [3]. (3) TALE motivates temporal weighting, while collapse research distinguishes directional alignment from low-dimensional representations. Neither supports interpreting embedding cosine similarity as recommendation diversity [4–5].

### Framework and candidates

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed experiment |
|---|---|---|
| Candidate discrimination | BCE; sampled cross-entropy | Uniform multi-negative CE |
| Current, specific intent | SASRec; candidate attention | Bounded recent-history residual |
| Persistent interests | Recurrence weighting | Recency versus recurrence ablation |
| Representation diagnosis | Mean cosine | Centered effective rank and margins |

Scores below use originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder. Each assessment gives a strength (+) and limitation (−).

| Idea | Scores | Assessment in score order |
|---|---|---|
| A: Uniform multi-negative CE [1–2] | 3/7/4/9/2 | +Controlled −Established; +Reusable −Incremental; +Sharper ranking −No temporal mechanism; +Targets weak margins −Training proxy; +Small change −Sampling care |
| **B: CE plus bounded candidate-conditioned recency residual [1–4]** | **5/8/8/8/5** | +Focused combination −Known components; +Extensible −Amazon uncertain; +Specific/current relevance −No satisfaction labels; +Candidate separation −May overfit; +Small branch −Catalog scoring cost |
| C: Recurrence-weighted residual [4] | 4/7/6/6/4 | +Controlled recurrence test −Close to starting idea; +Persistent-intent modeling −Sparse repeats; +Recurring tastes −Stale-demand risk; +Richer features −Indirect margin effect; +Simple pooling −Weight tuning |

### Selected idea: B

At 10% progress, B balances feasibility and diagnostic coverage. It explicitly targets **broad associations outranking specific matches** through candidate-conditioned history extraction and **stale interests displacing current priorities** through learned recency decay. These are hypotheses, not observed compatibility or satisfaction labels. Multi-negative CE targets Electronics’ 12.55% and Industrial’s 10.33% training negative-win rates; these do not establish validation performance.

Pseudocode: `h=SASRec(prefix); r=Attention(candidate, causal_history, recency_bias); score=h·candidate + bounded_residual(r,candidate); loss=CE(positive, uniform_negatives)`.

Run sequential ablations: baseline, CE, CE+recency residual, then recurrence replacement. Match negative counts and compute when comparing residuals. Select solely by four-category macro validation HR@10. Preserve routing, seeds, splits, predictor serialization and diagnostic interfaces; chunk full-catalog candidates. Use only training histories and available metadata, with no target-time features.

References: [1] gSASRec; [2] Scalable Cross-Entropy; [3] VISTA; [4] TALE; [5] On the Embedding Collapse when Scaling up Recommendation Models. Links appear below.

idea.description: Add a norm-bounded, candidate-conditioned recent-history residual to causal SASRec, trained with uniform multi-negative candidate-set cross-entropy. Establish the objective-only result before evaluating the residual.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies insufficiently specific matches and stale interests dominating current priorities. Candidate-conditioned attention and recency weighting explicitly target those two failures. Candidate competition targets the comparatively weak sampled training separation in Electronics and Industrial_and_Scientific. Improvements remain hypotheses until measured with pinned macro validation HR@10.
idea.implementation_notes: At each training position, attend only to the available prefix. Use learned ID embeddings initially; leave a from-scratch title/description encoder as a later independent ablation. Normalize the attention summary and candidate vector, and bound the added score by beta*tanh(g), with a small beta selected on validation. Compute attention logits from candidate-history compatibility plus a nonnegative learned positional decay. Initialize the residual gate near zero. Draw uniform negatives excluding padding and known training positives; define the resulting loss as candidate-set CE, without claiming unbiased full-softmax estimation. Tune the negative count within the shared GPU budget. Compare baseline, objective-only, recency residual and recurrence residual sequentially, retaining all four datasets. Do not use held-out interactions to construct histories, negative exclusions or recurrence statistics. Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and artifacts beneath the trial directory. Update the predictor writer to serialize architecture configuration and weights and reproduce candidate-conditioned scoring with chunked candidates. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Since scoring becomes candidate-dependent, adapt margin probes to call view.predict_score(features, items) independently for positive and negative candidates while retaining causal history in features. Preserve view.model as the trained module and the remaining compatibility attributes. Report training margins separately from validation HR@10; supplement cosine alignment with centered effective rank if budget allows. No implementation or experiment was executed in this response.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category, using preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42:
  Train baseline SASRec and then the uniform multi-negative CE ablation.
  For each valid training position t:
    H = causal SASRec states through t
    h = H[t]
    C = [next_positive] + K uniform eligible negatives
    For candidate c in C:
      a = softmax(query(e[c]) @ key(H).T / sqrt(d)
                  - softplus(decay) * positional_age)
      r = normalize(a @ value(H))
      residual = beta * tanh(gate(h)) * dot(r, normalize(e[c]))
      score[c] = dot(h, e[c]) + residual
    loss = cross_entropy(score, positive_index=0)
    Update parameters.
  Evaluate with the unchanged pinned validation procedure.
Compare recency and recurrence residuals at equal K and matched compute.
Select the configuration by four-category macro validation HR@10.
Write matching architecture, checkpoints and working/predict.py.

originality.positive: Combines candidate-specific recent-interest extraction, an explicitly bounded residual and a controlled objective ablation around the observed failures.
originality.negative: Candidate attention, temporal weighting and multi-negative cross-entropy each have established precedents.

future_potential.positive: Provides a controlled foundation for testing recurrence and locally trained text features while distinguishing objective gains from representation gains.
future_potential.negative: Sparse Amazon histories may not support reliable candidate attention, and no validation improvement has been demonstrated.

code_difficulty.positive: Retains the SASRec backbone and adds a small attention and scoring branch.
code_difficulty.negative: Requires candidate-dependent diagnostic scoring, causal masking, chunked catalog inference and synchronized predictor serialization.

related_work.title: gSASRec (2024 extended abstract)
contributions: Identifies overconfidence associated with negative-sampled BCE, motivating an objective-first ablation.
limitations: Does not establish that uniform candidate-set CE or the proposed residual improves this benchmark.

related_work.title: Scalable Cross-Entropy (RecSys 2024)
contributions: Approximates catalog cross-entropy using informative high-scoring items.
limitations: Its sampling approach differs from the proposed uniform candidate-set objective.

related_work.title: VISTA
contributions: Uses cached history tokens with candidate-conditioned attention to extract candidate-specific preferences.
limitations: Industrial-scale results do not establish gains on short Amazon histories or exact compatibility reasoning.

related_work.title: TALE
contributions: Motivates temporal weighting of transitions and attention to changing popularity.
limitations: Temporal interaction patterns do not reveal whether a purchase satisfied a need.

related_work.title: On the Embedding Collapse when Scaling up Recommendation Models
contributions: Characterizes collapse through occupation of a low-dimensional embedding subspace.
limitations: Mean cosine alignment alone cannot establish collapse, recommendation diversity or the cause of weak ranking.
